description: We are the “Los Lunares” team, a diverse group made up of an industrial engineer, students pursuing degrees in Telecommunications Engineering, Cybersecurity, Physics, and Renewable Energy, as well as a high school student with computer science knowledge. We are united by one mission: to give NASA researchers eyes on the Moon.
summary:
Los Lunares is an interactive web platform developed using real data obtained from NASA databases, designed to facilitate the analysis and planning of future lunar missions. It features a dual interface: a professional interface, aimed at experts and researchers, which allows users to evaluate potential landing sites, solar illumination, energy generation, and communication with Earth; and an educational interface, designed for the general public, where young people can have fun playing games, overcoming challenges, and learning about space exploration through a simulated lunar mission.
The project also aims to store these contributions in its own database to organize and validate information that could be useful to researchers and future NASA studies.
The goal is to bring together science, technology, and entertainment, facilitating lunar analysis while turning fun and learning into an opportunity to contribute to scientific knowledge and future space missions.
details:
The platform features two main interfaces: a professional interface designed for researchers, engineers, and specialists, and an educational interface aimed at the general public, particularly young people and students.

For more information, please visit the following link. https://drive.google.com/file/d/1rKNXke1hkG4M3ADP-fS3feze-9RW589-/view?usp=sharing

Professional Interface: Analysis of Potential Landing Sites

It allows users to explore lunar topographic maps and identify terrain features such as craters, slopes, rocks, obstacles, and relatively flat surfaces that may influence the selection of a landing site.

It also analyzes the position of the Sun relative to the local lunar horizon to determine periods of illumination and darkness, estimate energy generation through photovoltaic panels, and assess battery storage requirements.

Likewise, it examines the position of Earth relative to the lunar horizon to identify visibility windows and opportunities for direct communication. This allows users to compare different locations and dates, evaluating terrain conditions, energy availability, and communication possibilities for a mission.

Educational Interface: Learning Through Play

Designed especially for young people and students, this interface allows participants to take on the role of lunar mission leaders, making decisions about landing sites, available energy, and communication with Earth.

Through questions, challenges, true-or-false activities, and mini-games, they learn concepts related to physics, astronomy, and renewable energy while having fun. At the end, a simulation demonstrates the mission's outcome, which can either succeed or fail depending on the decisions made.

The goal is to transform complex scientific concepts into accessible experiences, spark curiosity, and encourage interest in scientific and technological careers.

Citizen Science

The platform incorporates collaborative mini-games inspired by CAPTCHA systems, allowing users to identify and classify features in real images of the lunar surface, such as craters, rocks, slopes, and obstacles.

Benefits and Long-Term Prospects

Los Lunares aims to facilitate the preliminary analysis of potential lunar landing sites, integrate scientific information into a single platform, and promote the use of solar energy in space environments. It also seeks to democratize access to knowledge, strengthen science education, and enable people without specialized training to participate in citizen science activities.

In the long term, the project aims to expand its analysis and simulation tools, incorporate additional lunar regions, and develop its own database to store participants' responses. These contributions will be compared to identify patterns and validate classifications. The platform also aims to implement a system for evaluating correct and incorrect answers to progressively improve results.

Furthermore, the project intends to develop scalable infrastructure, including a structured database and a web server capable of supporting the platform's growth and accommodating thousands of simultaneous users. The collected information could become a valuable complementary resource for researchers and future studies related to lunar exploration.

These tools will help evaluate different scenarios for future missions. However, their results will be indicative and will not replace the technical studies or safety assessments required for an actual space mission.

Project Vision

The innovation behind Los Lunares lies in combining scientific research, technology, renewable energy, education, and citizen participation within a single platform. Its purpose is to provide specialists with tools to analyze the lunar environment, while young people learn through interactive experiences and the public contributes to the generation of scientific information.

Los Lunares aims to become a bridge between science and society, promoting knowledge, innovation, and interest in future space missions. Because exploring the Moon is not simply about reaching it, but also about understanding it, learning from it, and paving the way for those who will continue exploring it.
